question: A 19-year-old male soccer player undergoes an exercise tolerance test to measure his maximal oxygen uptake during exercise. Which of the following changes are most likely to occur during exercise?

options.opd: Increased arterial partial pressure of oxygen

analysis: During exercise, the body's demand for oxygen increases, leading to various physiological changes to meet this demand. Increased pulmonary vascular resistance would be counterproductive as it would impede blood flow to the lungs for oxygenation. Decreased physiologic dead space allows for more efficient gas exchange by reducing the volume of air that does not participate in gas exchange. Decreased alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient indicates improved oxygen transfer from the alveoli to the blood. Increased arterial partial pressure of oxygen reflects enhanced oxygen uptake. Increased apical ventilation-perfusion ratio may occur to optimize gas exchange in the lungs.
